question: Assume today is 2026-09-08. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total number of A&E attendances in England in September 2026 (all A&E types, including minor injury units and walk-in centres), as reported in NHS England's monthly A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions statistics.

target.what: Total number of A&E attendances (all A&E types, including major A&E departments, single-specialty A&E, minor injury units and walk-in centres) in England during September 2026, as reported in NHS England's monthly A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions statistics (count of attendances, not unique
target.publisher: NHS England (A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions monthly statistics)
target.caveats: Target period is future/ongoing relative to the 2026-09-08 cutoff, so no September 2026 data exist yet; must be forecast from prior months, seasonality, and trends. Working interpretation: all A&E types combined (type 1 major, type 2 single-specialty, type 3 minor injury/walk-in/other), total attend

methods.label: m1

p43.role: Total all-type A&E attendances in England, July 2026

methods.rationale: Carries the most recent published all-type monthly total (July 2026) into September 2026 using a seasonal/trend ratio. Shared dependency: relies on p43 being a clean all-type total and on the seasonal pattern being stable; failure mode is an unusual September surge or a definitional change in the series.

methods.label: m2

p58.role: Total all-type A&E attendances in England, September 2025

a2.role: September 2026 to September 2025 year-on-year growth factor

methods.rationale: Uses the same-month prior-year total (September 2025) scaled by a y/y growth factor grounded in recent growth evidence (p46, p108, p109, p14). Shared dependency: p58 is a rounded press figure; failure mode is a break in the growth trend or a change in reporting scope.

methods.label: m3
methods.rationale: Naive carry-forward of the most recent September total (2025) as a baseline; it ignores trend but provides a low-variance anchor and backtests the seasonal level. Failure mode: misses the recent upward trend.

kept.name: September 2026 to July 2026 seasonal/trend ratio
kept.rationale: September typically runs slightly below the July summer peak in all-type attendances; with a modest upward trend into autumn, a ratio near 0.96 is plausible. Range reflects uncertainty in both seasonality and trend.
kept.applies_when: The July 2026 level (p43) is a valid base and September 2026 follows the recent seasonal pattern.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 attendances exceed July 2026 or fall more than 10% below it.

kept.name: September 2026 vs September 2025 year-on-year growth factor
kept.rationale: Recent y/y growth has been around 3% (p46, p108, p109, p14), and September 2025 was itself up ~7% on 2024 (p62); a 3% growth factor is consistent with the recent trend, with a range spanning flat to 7%.
kept.applies_when: September 2025 (p58) is a valid base and the recent low-single-digit growth trend continues.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp acceleration or contraction in A&E demand in mid/late 2026.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
